_comment: TEMPLATE, not the live file. Nothing in this repo reads it. The file every Paseo skill actually reads is ~/.paseo/orchestration-preferences.json; on the machine that runs agents, `cp examples/orchestration-preferences.json ~/.paseo/`. JSON has no comment syntax, so the reasoning lives in the `_`-prefixed keys below; the skills read `providers` and `preferences` and ignore the rest.
_contract: skills/paseo/SKILL.md, 'Orchestration preferences'. `providers` maps the five role categories to provider strings passed straight to create_agent's `provider` field; `preferences` is a freeform string array read at startup and woven into agent prompts. Categories are fixed by that skill: impl, ui, research, planning, audit.
_unverified: Written on a machine with no Paseo and no ~/.paseo, so nothing here was dispatched then. Partly closed on 2026-09-04 on a host with paseo 0.7.2: `claude/opus` and `codex/gpt-5.6-sol` were dispatched and inspected and come up as claude-opus-5 and gpt-5.6-sol; `codex/gpt-5.6-luna` still has not been. Every provider string is copied verbatim from an attested id (the examples in skills/paseo/SKILL.md, or an id in models.json, whose ids are <Provider>/<Model> per bin/bus match_observed). A string being well-formed is not proof an agent comes up on that model: confirm on the host with `paseo run` + `paseo inspect`, or launch through `bus launch-worker`, which inspects the agent it created and stops it when provider, model, thinking id, cwd or branch differ from the plan, or check a worker someone else launched with `bus await --expect-provider/--expect-model/--expect-thinking`. The two subcommands that exist are `bus launch-worker` and `bus await`; earlier text here named a third one, which does not. Also verified on 2026-09-24: `paseo run --provider codex --model gpt-6-astra --thinking high` inspected as Provider codex, Model gpt-6-astra, Thinking high, and the agent answered, before codex/gpt-6-astra became the impl default.
preferences: Reasoning effort is per MODEL: codex/gpt-6-astra at high (the impl default since 2026-09-24), codex/gpt-5.6-sol at high, codex/gpt-5.6-luna at xhigh, claude/opus at high. luna sits below the other two on measured intelligence, so it is asked for xhigh to compensate; asking the leaders for xhigh buys latency, not quality. This file CANNOT set it -- `providers` values are provider strings only, and effort is a separate axis (`paseo run --thinking <id>`, or settings.thinkingOptionId on create_agent). So treat this as the intent to pass through, not as configuration that takes effect. hanig-swarm enforces it for its own code units in swarm.py's THINKING_BY_MODEL; a paseo skill dispatching from these categories gets the PROVIDER default instead, measured on 2026-09-04 as xhigh for codex and auto for claude -- so claude/opus in the ui and planning seats silently runs BELOW the intent, and codex/gpt-5.6-sol ran above it when it held impl, unless the dispatcher passes --thinking. The bare default for codex/gpt-6-astra, impl since 2026-09-24, is UNMEASURED; do not assume it matches sol's, and pass --thinking high explicitly, as hanig-swarm's THINKING_BY_MODEL already does. What this file cannot configure, bin/bus can verify: launch with `bus launch-worker --thinking <id>`, which re-inspects the agent it created and stops it on a mismatch, or check a running agent with `bus await --expect-thinking <id>`, which exits 4 on a mismatch. Verification is the backstop and not the fix: it catches a wrong effort, it does not set one.

Astra (codex/gpt-6-astra, thinking high) drives coding agents, by owner decision on 2026-09-24; it replaced Sol. The author rule is unchanged and now binds Astra: the model that wrote a change does not review it, so never seat the impl provider in a gate-review or audit seat for work it wrote. No gate tier contains Astra: Sol took its deep-tier seat on 2026-09-24, so escalating an Astra-authored change adds a non-author.

A real review gate is `review.py` over `reviewers.json` (kimi-k2.7-code, luna, glm-5.3) - three models across two API providers, prompted to refute. A single `audit` agent launched from this file is one opinion and is not a substitute for it.

Committee work is `committee.py` (luna, deepseek, kimi; 2-3 members). DeepSeek plans well and concedes under challenge but over-claims as a refuter, so it sits on the committee and in no gate profile.
Claude Opus is the right choice for anything artistic or human-skill-oriented: copywriting, naming, UX copy, visual design, styling. Codex is the workhorse for mechanical work.

When the category leaves room, or the user asks for efficient routing, run `~/.agent-bus/bin/bus models --json` and take the cheapest model that clears the bar. DeepSeek Flash is text-only: never send it images.

_judgement_calls.impl: SETTLED, amended 2026-09-24 by the owner: coding agents are codex/gpt-6-astra at thinking high, replacing codex/gpt-5.6-sol from the 2026-09-01 decision. Verified on a live agent before adoption: paseo inspect showed Provider codex, Model gpt-6-astra, Thinking high, and the agent answered.
_judgement_calls.ui: CARRIED FORWARD, not re-decided. The 2026-09-01 decision says nothing about UI. claude/opus is the standing preference from the example in skills/paseo/SKILL.md and the note on claude/opus in models.json ('UI/design/artistic judgment per orchestration preferences').
_judgement_calls.planning: JUDGEMENT CALL. The decision says Sol coordinates and integrates, which reads like planning - but paseo-committee draws its members from the planning and research categories, and its Phase 3 sends those same members the implementation diff to review. With the impl provider in a planning slot, the author is back in the review seat, which is the one thing the decision forbids. So planning is claude/opus: highest intelligence index in models.json (60.7) and a different provider from impl. Note this key does NOT select the decided committee (luna, deepseek, kimi) - that roster lives in reviewers.json's `committee` profile and runs through committee.py over API providers, a different mechanism from paseo-committee.
_judgement_calls.research: JUDGEMENT CALL. codex/gpt-5.6-luna: luna sits on both the decided gate and the decided committee, so a luna research agent is consistent with the roster, and models.json credits it with stronger instruction following and image-capable inspection. Pairing it with claude/opus in planning also gives paseo-committee two providers to contrast, mirroring 'across two providers'. Counter-evidence, recorded rather than hidden: models.json calls kimi the 'default audit/research provider per orchestration preferences'. Kimi is not used here only because its single-string form is unverifiable - see _unmapped.kimi.
_judgement_calls.audit: JUDGEMENT CALL, but the negative half is settled. NOT the impl provider (codex/gpt-6-astra since 2026-09-24; codex/gpt-5.6-sol before): the model that writes the code does not review it. Of the three decided gate models (kimi-k2.7-code, luna, glm-5.3), luna is the only one with an attested Paseo provider string. This key cannot express a three-model panel at all - see _unmapped.gate_and_committee_are_not_paseo.

_unmapped.thinking: Effort has no slot in this schema, and bin/bus can assert one at launch instead. Measured live on this host on 2026-09-04 (paseo 0.7.2) by dispatching real agents and inspecting them: a bare `--provider claude/opus` comes up Model=claude-opus-5, Thinking=auto, against an intent of high -- so ui and planning run BELOW intent; a bare `--provider codex/gpt-5.6-sol` comes up Thinking=xhigh against an intent of high, so impl runs above it; codex/gpt-5.6-luna was NOT dispatched -- the registry claims xhigh for it, which would be research's and audit's intent, right by accident, but see the trap below before trusting that. Passing `--thinking high` to claude/opus does take (inspected Thinking=high), so the axis works, it is simply never passed. Trap: `paseo provider models claude` advertises defaultThinkingOptionId=high for claude-opus-5 while a real dispatch lands on auto, which is not even in that model's thinkingOptionIds -- read effort off an inspected agent, never off the registry. Enforced only where the dispatcher passes it: swarm.py does, the paseo skills do not.
_unmapped.thinking_high: The decision's 'thinking high' is create_agent `settings.thinkingOptionId` / `paseo run --thinking high`, and this file has no slot for it. It is stated in `preferences` so it reaches prompts, but this file does not enforce it. The check that does exist is bin/bus's launch contract: `launch_contract_issues` compares `paseo inspect`'s `Thinking` field against `--expect-thinking`. Exercised on 2026-09-04 against a live pair of claude/opus agents: exit 0 for the one launched with `--thinking high`, exit 4 and `unmet: thinking=auto; expected high` for the bare one.
_unmapped.deepseek: The committee's DeepSeek reaches Paseo as provider `pi` with model `deepseek-runai/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` - two fields (skills/start-a-sprint/SKILL.md; models.json, which warns the bare id times out Paseo's pi adapter). A category value is a single string, so that route cannot be written here. Left out rather than guessed: use committee.py, or pass provider and model explicitly.
_unmapped.kimi: models.json ids are <Provider>/<Model>, so its kimi entry `kimi/kimi-code/k3-256k` is provider `kimi` plus model `kimi-code/k3-256k`. Whether create_agent's single `provider` field accepts the concatenated three-segment string is not verifiable without a daemon. It is a candidate to test on the host and adopt for `research`/`audit` if it works - not used above rather than guessed.
_unmapped.glm-5.3: A decided gate model with no Paseo route anywhere in this repo: reviewers.json reaches it over OpenRouter as `z-ai/glm-5.3`. No Paseo provider string for it is attested here, and none is invented.
_unmapped.gate_and_committee_are_not_paseo: 'The review gate is kimi-k2.7-code, luna and glm-5.3' and 'the committee is luna, deepseek and kimi' describe profiles in skills/hanig-review-gate/reviewers.json, executed by review.py and committee.py against API endpoints. This file routes Paseo-launched agents, one provider string per role. The rosters are already encoded where they run; `audit` here is a one-agent approximation of the gate, not the gate.
